text_blocks.snippet: Scam trends in Central Illinois include fake law enforcement calls, utility threats, and tech or AI-driven impersonations.

list.snippet: Sheriff Impersonators: Scammers spoof local sheriff numbers (such as in Tazewell County) claiming you missed jury duty or have a warrant, demanding immediate payment to avoid arrest. Law enforcement never calls demanding cash or gift cards over the phone.
I-PASS and DMV Phishing: Text messages claim you owe unpaid tolls or that your license is suspended via fake Illinois Secretary of State alerts.
AI and Impersonation Trends: The Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois reports a rise in AI-aided family and celebrity impersonation, tech support traps, and fake romantic connections.
Door-to-Door Charity Fraud: Local groups like the Champaign YMCA have warned about individuals going door-to-door using fake logos to solicit unauthorized cash donations.
Cryptocurrency ATMs: Scammers direct victims in cities like Springfield to local crypto ATMs to deposit cash under high-pressure pretenses.
Practice the pause: Take a breath when someone demands instant money, secrecy, or panic-driven action.
Never click links in texts: Delete unsolicited messages about tolls, DMV fees, or package deliveries with unknown QR codes ("brushing" scams).
Verify independently: Look up official phone numbers yourself rather than using numbers provided in suspicious texts or calls.

text_blocks.snippet: If you suspect you've been targeted or want to check a specific message you received, tell me what the communication claimed so I can help you verify its legitimacy.
